Article Title: 105, not out? SC orders release of murder convict
Article Text:
SC permanently releases 105-year-old life convict Rasik Mandal, says he should spend his remaining days with family

Born in 1920 when Congress had launched the non-cooperation movement against the British, Rasik Mandal got his freedom as a 105-year-old life convict Friday after SC ordered the centenarian should spend his remaining days with his family. He was convicted in 1994 for a 1988 murder. On Friday, the bench first asked: "Is he alive? Why should he not be released permanently? Why should he be on interim parole?"Born in a nondescript village of Malda district, Rasik Chandra was arrested in 1988 for murder at the age of 68, and convicted in Dec 1994.His appeal against conviction was dismissed by Calcutta HC in 2018, after 24 years, and Supreme Court rejected his appeal in 2019.Serving a life sentence, he was shifted to a correctional home at Balurghat in West Bengal from prison due to age-related ailments. Mandal, through his son, had filed a writ petition in SC in 2020, when he was just short of the century-mark, seeking premature release on ground of age and related ailments. On Nov 29, 2024, SC admitted Mandal’s petition and directed his release “on interim bail/parole in the case lodged on Nov 9, 1988, at Manikchak police station in WB’s Malda”.On Friday, as the Supreme Court bench wondered why he should not be released, the West Bengal counsel said the court could direct that he would not be incarcerated any longer. “Having regard to his age, we see no reason not to release him. We allow his writ petition while making the Nov 29, 2024, order absolute. He is permanently released from jail for the purpose of this case,” the apex court said.
Article Summary: Rasik Chandra Mandal was arrested in 1988 for murder at the age of 68, and convicted in Dec 1994. Mandal, through his son, had filed a writ petition in SC in 2020, when he was just short of the century-mark, seeking premature release. On Nov 29, 2024, SC admitted Mandal’s petition and directed his release “on interim bail/parole in the case lodged on Nov 9, 1988, at Manikchak police station in Malda”

Article Title: 'Rahul's mohabbat ki dukan': BJP slams Congress' tributes to anti-Sikh riots accused Sajjan Kumar
Article Text:
Sajjan Kumar was sevring life imprisonment in Delhi's Tihar Jail

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Friday hit back at the Congress after several of its leaders paid tribute to former party leader Sajjan Kumar, a convict in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, who died at 80 Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar, a former three-term Lok Sabha MP, as an "irreparable loss.""Today, the country's political landscape has suffered an irreparable loss... Sajjan Kumar ji was a leader whose connection with people in Delhi and across north India was cited as a model across the country," he said.Reacting to Hooda's remarks, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community", referring to Kumar's role in the anti-Sikh riots."Congress calls late Sajjan Kumar, a man convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, a 'role model'! How can Congress eulogise the killers of our Sikh community?" Bhandari posted on X."This is the real mindset of 'Mohabbat Ki Dukkan' (shop of love) of Rahul Gandhi and exposes the innate hate Congress has for the Sikh community!" Bhandari added, referring to a phrase used by Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha.The BJP spokesperson further demanded that Congress apologise for "insulting" the victims of the anti-Sikh riots and "rubbing" salt into the wounds of the survivors and victims' families.Congress leader Udit Raj also described Kumar's death as a "great loss" for the party."It is a great loss for the Congress. He was a very senior Congress leader, and it will be difficult to fill the void... He did a lot of work, especially for the poor," Raj stated.Sajjan Kumar died at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital on Thursday."Sajjan Kumar was brought to Safdarjung Hospital by police with altered sensorium around 11 am. He was immediately admitted and resuscitation measures were initiated. Despite providing all necessary medical and life-support measures, he could not be saved and passed away at 12:30 pm," the hospital's statement read."He was a known case of high blood pressure and Parkinson's disease and had a history of multiple hospital admissions in the past," the statement added.Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.He was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots.He was also sentenced to life imprisonment by a Delhi court in February 2025 in another case relating to the killing of two Sikh men during the riots.Kumar resigned from the primary membership of the Congress after the 2018 conviction.
Article Summary: Congress MP Deepender Hooda described the death of Kumar as an "irreparable loss" BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused the Congress of "eulogising the killers of the Sikh community" Kumar was serving multiple life sentences after his conviction in cases linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.

Article Title: SC scraps SAD chief Badal’s plea to quash 2017 defamation case over linking AKJ with terror outfit
Article Text:
SC dismisses Sukhbir Badal's plea against defamation case over BKI-AKJ remarks

What's the case?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to interfere with criminal defamation proceedings against Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal over alleged remarks linking religious organisation Akhand Kirtani Jatha (AKJ) with banned terrorist outfit Babbar Khalsa International (BKI).A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed Badal’s challenge. The proceedings were initiated by Rajinder Pal Singh, an AKJ member who alleged that the former minister’s remarks damaged his reputation by associating him with the banned organisation."We have read this order. What is alleged against you (Badal)? You say that this organisation is a terrorist organisation and this complainant is the spokesperson of the other organisation which is the political front...," the bench said.According to PTI, advocate appearing for Badal said, "He (complainant) says he is the spokesperson. We don't know who has authorised him."The bench then dismissed the plea.The controversy dates back to the 2017 Punjab Assembly elections, when then Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal visited Singh’s residence. Badal had subsequently accused Kejriwal of reaching out to “radicals” in Punjab, according to the allegations in the complaint.A Chandigarh magistrate later took cognisance of the complaint and summoned Badal. Badal challenged the proceedings before the Punjab and Haryana High Court, but the court rejected his plea in October 2025.Badal then approached the Supreme Court, which on Friday found no ground to interfere with the pending proceedings, news agency ANI reported.
Article Summary: SC dismisses Sukhbir Badal's plea against defamation case over BKI-AKJ remarks. The proceedings were initiated by Rajinder Pal Singh, an AKJ member who alleged that the former minister’s remarks damaged his reputation by associating him with the banned organisation.

NEW DELHI: High-voltage drama unfolded at Delhi's Parliament Street police station on Friday after Rahul Gandhi claimed that police refused to register a complaint over the "police brutality" during July 20 student protest at Jantar Mantar.According to Congress sources quoted by news agency ANI, Lochab, along with his lawyers, approached the Delhi Police on August 14 and submitted a written complaint.However, the police allegedly did not provide an I/O number or acknowledgement. The complaint was followed up again on August 17 through email and phone, but no I/O number or acknowledgement was provided.On Friday, Rahul accompanied Lochab to the DCP office to seek action on the complaint and press for registration of an FIR. They alleged that the DCP again did not provide details of the case officer or the I/O number.The complaint relates to police action and excessive use of force, including the alleged firing of pellet guns, against student protesters during the July 20 demonstration in Delhi.According to the complainant, the incident amounts to a cognisable offence and warrants registration of an FIR. Rahul has sought action on the complaint and demanded justice for Lochab.The Congress leader had gone to the DCP office at the police station along with Sahil Lochab, who was injured in a police crackdown during the students' "Sansad Chalo" march over the NEET paper fiasco.After meeting senior police officials, Rahul came out of the police station and said Sahil had not been allowed to file an FIR."Sahil wants to file FIR for justice, but that is not being allowed," Rahul said.Soon after coming out of the police station, Rahul staged a sit-in outside the premises with Sahil. His sister and Congress colleague Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined his dharna minutes later.Visuals from the DCP office showed Rahul discussing the matter with police officials as pellet-gun victim Sahil, standing beside him.Scenes from parliament street police station also showed immediate deployment of Rapid Action Force.Lok Sabha leader of opposition accused the authorities of undermining constitutional principles, saying that by refusing to register the FIR, "the Constitution being trampled."Rahul, however, vowed to fight for justice for Sahil and other students who were injured during the protest.He said he would "ensure justice for pellet victim Sahil and every student like him."In a post on X, the Rae Bareli MP said Sahil was severely injured during the "police brutality" during the July 20 "Sansad chalo" march organised by students over the NEET paper leak.Rahul said, " Sahil's vision in one eye is now at risk."He added, "Such brutality against a peaceful protest is not just illegal—it's a serious crime. Neither has home minister Amit Shah offered any explanation to the students for this cruelty, nor has the Prime Minister apologized to them."Directly targeting Union home minister Amit Shah, who oversees the functioning of the Delhi Police, Rahul wrote: "Amit Shah ji, why are you so scared of justice? This fear shows that you are admitting to your crime."Doubling down on his demand for justice, Rahul said, "The FIR will be filed. A judicial inquiry will take place. And action will be taken against everyone, from top to bottom, who is guilty of this brutality. We will ensure justice for Sahil, and every student victim like him."Talking to reporters outside the police station, Congress leader said, "Look at this pellet carefully. This is a pellet. Where did these pellets come from? They came from his (Sahil Lochav) body. Look at these pellets lodged in his body. There are more than 200 pellets in his body. These are AIIMS and Lady Hardinge Hospital reports, which clearly state that there are more than 200 pellets in his body."Lok Sabha LoP added, "There are three pellets in his eye, and he has lost vision in that eye. He will not be able to see through that eye. There are also pellets lodged very close to his heart, which cannot be removed. Delhi Police has said that they did not fire the pellets. So, there is only one question: If you did not fire them, then someone must have fired these pellets. Perhaps someone else fired them at him. And if no one else fired them, then perhaps he fired the pellets at himself. "The victim, who was accompanying Rahul, also spoke to reporters and said, "On 20th July, pellet guns were fired at me. I was admitted to Lady Hardinge, from there, I was referred to AIIMS. I underwent surgery at AIIMS.But the vision in my eye is still not clear. On 14th August, I wrote a 7-page complaint and gave to my lawyer...But the FIR has not been registered."The dharna outside the police station in central Delhi was Rahul Gandhi's second protest against the crackdown. Weeks earlier, Rahul, along with Akhilesh Yadav, had marched towards PM Modi's residence at Lok Kalyan Marg, where the two leaders were briefly detained.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi claims police refused to register a complaint over "police brutality" during July 20 student protest at Jantar Mantar. Rahul has sought action on the complaint and demanded justice for Sahil Lochab. Lochab was injured in a police crackdown during the students' "Sansad Chalo" march over the NEET paper fiasco.

New Delhi: BJP Friday said Rahul Gandhi had orchestrated the "drama" of sitting on dharna in a police station as a diversionary ploy after Congress came under flak across the country over its stand on Vande Mataram ."Rahul manufactured this drama suddenly as a cover for his anti-national stand and to divert attention from this big embarrassment," Union minister J P Nadda said, as the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha staged a sit-in at Parliament Street police station."The country is again witnessing his cheap and diversionary politics," Nadda said as he questioned the need for the protest when Supreme Court had taken cognisance of a batch of petitions alleging police excesses on July 20 and had constituted a five-member committee headed by a retired judge to look into the matter."Does the leader of opposition have no faith in the judiciary? NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party's attempt to inspect a government school in Rajasthan triggered a political storm after party members alleged they were attacked while trying to visit a school they claimed had been operating from a buffalo shed for years."BJP goons have once again resorted to violence against our team. Article Title: Pellet injuries: FIR filed after Rahul Gandhi sits on dharna
Article Text:
Delhi Police registered a case after Rahul Gandhi staged a dharna.





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police registered a case after leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi staged a five-hour dharna outside Parliament Street police station Friday, demanding an FIR in connection with pellet injuries suffered by 19-year-old Sahil Lochab during the July 20 Jantar Mantar protest, reports Abhay.Gandhi reached the police station with Lochab, his mother and their lawyer around 11.30am. He was later joined by Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other party functionaries, and met the DCP and other senior officers.Displaying Lochab’s medical reports, Gandhi said more than 200 pellets had entered the student’s body, including three that struck his eye and put his vision at risk. Some pellets, he added, were lodged near Lochab’s heart and could not be removed by doctors. He also displayed a pellet recovered from the student’s body during treatment.“Brutality against a peaceful protest is a serious crime. An offence has been committed and we are demanding registration of an FIR,” Gandhi said, alleging Delhi Police told them they had received instructions “from above” not to register the case. The charge was denied by police.After over five hours, Lochab’s complaint was filed and an FIR registered against unknown persons under sections 118(1) and 125 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous means and acts endangering life or personal safety.Gandhi termed it “a first step towards justice”. Thanking him, Lochab said: “When he called to ask about my health, I mentioned that my FIR wasn’t being registered. He immediately said, ‘Let’s meet tomorrow; I will go and get your FIR filed.’ It took eight hours to get the FIR registered, and perhaps it wouldn’t have been registered at all if the LOP hadn’t supported me.”According to Lochab, he submitted a seven-page complaint to police on Aug 14 seeking registration of an FIR, but no action was taken.In his complaint, Lochab, a Najafgarh resident, said he had joined the July 20 Sansad Chalo march against the alleged NEET paper leak. He alleged that when the lathicharge and teargas firing began, he ran with the crowd towards Connaught Place, but as he approached Palika Bazaar and Connaught Place carrying the tricolour, he was hit multiple times by metal pellets fired by a person in a blue uniform carrying a large gun.Lochab stated that he suffered injuries to his right eye, face, arm and chest, and lost vision in his right eye. He was taken to Lady Hardinge Hospital and later referred to Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS. His first eye surgery was performed on July 22. He said his MLC recorded that the eye injury was caused by a pellet and that the chances of recovery were less than 1%.An AIIMS CT scan showed more than 200 pellets lodged in his body, including in his eye, neck, chest, jaw and arm, Lochab stated, adding some pellets near the eye nerve could not be removed. He underwent a second eye surgery on Aug 1, but his vision had not returned, he added.Lochab also said the injuries had disrupted his studies and ended his hopes of joining Delhi Police. In his complaint, he sought preservation of CCTV and drone footage, forensic examination of the pellets removed from his body and registration of an FIR.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi staged a five-hour dharna outside Parliament Street police station. He was demanding an FIR in connection with pellet injuries suffered by 19-year- old Sahil Lochab. Gandhi said more than 200 pellets had entered the student’s body, including three that struck his eye.

Article Title: Ambernath BJP-MNS clash: Case registered against 2 BJP corporators, five others
Article Text:
A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash.





AMBERNATH: The political clash between BJP and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) workers in Ambernath has taken a fresh turn, with Shivaji Nagar police registering a fresh case against seven people, including two BJP corporators, on the complaint of an MNS worker who was injured in the incident.The latest case was registered on Sunday on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash. Police have booked BJP corporators Abhijit Karanjule and Pawan Walekar along with five others under sections 118(1), 115(2), 189(2), 190, 191(2) and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The development comes days after police arrested Shirke and some of his associates for allegedly assaulting BJP office-bearer Laxmi Narayan Chauhan at his office in Vadavali.A subsequent clash between BJP and MNS workers at Shivaji Nagar police station further escalated tensions.MNS leaders had alleged that police took one-sided action by arresting their office-bearers while failing to act against BJP workers allegedly involved in the assault on Shirke. MNS leader Avinash Jadhav had demanded action against those responsible.Following the demand, MNS district president Bandu Deshmukh had announced a protest on Sunday against what the party termed one-sided police action. However, after police registered an FIR against BJP workers, MNS withdrew its protest.
Article Summary: A new case was filed against seven individuals, including two BJP corporators, following a clash. The latest case was registered on the complaint of Suhas Ghag, a relative of MNS Ambernath city chief Shailesh Shirke, who was also injured in the clash.

Article Title: Nashik police bust sex racket, one woman rescued
Article Text:
Nashik:





The central crime branch of Nashik city police busted a sex racket that was operating under the guise of a fitness centre in the Mumbai Naka area.The raid was carried out by the anti-human trafficking unit (AHTU) on Wednesday, leading to the rescue of one woman.Acting on confidential information, officials learnt that illegal commercial sex activities were being carried out at a bungalow in an area under Mumbai Naka.The establishment was masquerading as an operational fitness centre. Upon verifying the information, the police raided the bungalow and confirmed the illicit operations.Following the raid, the Mumbai Naka police registered a case under sections of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act against two individuals, and rescued a woman who was pressed into prostitution by the two persons for their own benefit.The raid was executed under the directions of the Nashik city police Commissioner Sandeep Karnik, DCP (Crime) Kirankumar Chavan, and ACP (Crime) Sandeep Mitke. Senior police inspector Yogesh Deshmukh led the operation raid.
Article Summary: The central crime branch of Nashik city police busted a sex racket that was operating under the guise of a fitness centre in the Mumbai Naka area. The raid was carried out by the anti-human trafficking unit (AHTU) on Wednesday, leading to the rescue of one woman.

Article Title: In TN assembly: DMK questions Vijay’s shift in delimitation stand, TVK ministers reject charge
Article Text:
Chennai:





Leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s shift in his stand on delimitation, resulting in an intense debate in the state assembly on Friday. TVK ministers maintained that the party has not changed its position.Udhayanidhi flagged the issue, citing Vijay’s speech in Southern Zone Council meeting chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah on Thursday at Mamallapuram. He said the assembly resolution passed on Aug 12 sought a “freeze” on the total number of Lok Sabha seats at 543, but the demand was not mentioned in the chief minister’s speech at the SZC meeting. Udhayanidhi asked whether the CM and his govt had shifted from the anti-delimitation resolution passed by the House.PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna said the state govt has not changed its stand and that it was committed to freezing the current LS strength for another 25 years through special legislation. Law minister R Nirmalkumar echoed the stand. “I made the govt’s stand clear that we are against delimitation and want to maintain the existing LS strength at 543,” he said.Udhayanidhi said DMK too wants the current strength to be retained. If there is a change, Tamil Nadu’s share of representation in parliament should be maintained at 7.18 %, he said.Aadhav intervened and said there appears to be a change in DMK’s stand, not in TVK’s. He asked whether DMK would fully back the Aug 12 assembly resolution to protect the state’s autonomy. Former ministers K N Nehru and S Regupathy responded that DMK would never compromise on state autonomy. “We firmly want the state’s representation to be safeguarded at the present 7.18% ratio,” Nehru said.Nirmalkumar then demanded DMK to clarify whether they will oppose the delimitation bill or not in the parliament.Former CM Edappadi K Palaniswami joined the debate and backed the demand for “fair delimitation” as the constitutional freeze on LS seats was set to lapse after 2026, as the delimitation exercise was inevitable. “We should push for fair delimitation,” Palaniswami said.PMK MLA A Ganeshkumar also backed the demand. He alleged that VCK leader Thol Thirumavalavan had changed his stand from “fair delimitation” to “no delimitation”, while Nehru made a similar charge on Congress.Wrapping up the debate, Aadhav applauded DMK and AIADMK for their efforts to protect state autonomy. He urged all parties to stand united, rejecting any offer that BJP may make with a “hidden agenda”.
Article Summary: Opposition leader Udhayanidhi Stalin questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s shift in his stand on delimitation. TVK ministers maintained that the party has not changed its position. Former ministers K N Nehru and S Regupathy responded that DMK would never compromise on state autonomy.

Article Title: Former sub-registrar held in Meenakshi temple land case
Article Text:
Central Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former sub-registrar Anantharaman in connection with the alleged transferring and registering of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple property worth around Rs60 crore.





Madurai: Central Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former sub-registrar Anantharaman in connection with the alleged transferring and registering of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple property worth around Rs60 crore. It was the sixth arrest made by CCB in the case.According to police, a fraudulent patta transfer, allegedly carried out in 2016, was cancelled following objections. While related litigation was pending before Madras high court , a fresh document allegedly concealing key facts was registered at the Murappanadu sub-registrar office in 2021.Police investigations revealed that power deeds registered at Murappanadu and Vadamadurai sub-registrar offices played a crucial role in the alleged fraud. These power documents were allegedly used as the basis for subsequent registrations that facilitated the disputed property transactions.Anantharaman, who served as sub-registrar at Murappanadu when the disputed documents were registered, was taken into custody and remanded to judicial custody after being produced before a court on Thursday.CCB registered a case and is investigating 19 accused in connection with the fraud.Several people, including Rajkumar, Ilaiyaraja, then VAO Arasan, Kalikumar, and then tahsildar Anbalagan have already been arrested. Anbalagan was also placed under suspension following his arrest.Police are continuing their probe into the chain of transactions, including registration of power deeds and subsequent alleged fraudulent documents linked to the trust properties. The disputed property comprises Ashoka Villas bungalow and a two-acre garden located near Tallakulam-Alagarkovil Road.
Article Summary: Central Crime Branch (CCB) police have arrested former sub-registrar Anantharaman in connection with the alleged transferring and registering of Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple property worth around Rs60 crore. It was the sixth arrest made by CCB in the case.

Article Title: Don’t rush on Meenakshi temple works: Tamilisai
Article Text:
BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure the September 17 Meenakshi Amman temple consecration works are completed without altering its heritage and HR&CE doesn’t act on haste.





Madurai: BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan on Friday urged the Tamil Nadu govt not to rush renovation works at Meenakshi Amman temple ahead of its consecration next month, saying several works were yet to be completed.She told reporters said shortcomings were being pointed out “out of devotion, not hostility” and asked the govt to ensure the temple’s heritage was preserved. She criticised civic conditions in Madurai, alleging corruption even in garbage collection and urging the govt to act.Tamilisai welcomed the southern chief ministers’ conference, rejecting claims that the Union govt was indifferent to southern states. She said Union home minister Amit Shah was focusing on the region, and cited the proposed Godavari-Cauvery river-linking project.On criticism that chief minister Vijay had reversed his position on delimitation, Tamilisai defended his call for proportional representation. “What is your problem with him saying the correct proportion should be followed?” she asked.She urged parties not to politicise delimitation, saying it was also necessary to ensure women’s reservation. Shah had assured that Tamil Nadu’s representation would not be reduced, she said.Tamilisai questioned the govt’s decision to provide cars to legislators, asking why public money should be spent on MLAs who already owned vehicles.Asked whether Vijay had raised Cauvery issue at the chief ministers’ conference, she said he might have done so even if details had not emerged publicly. Tamil Nadu’s rights on Cauvery would not be compromised by either Vijay or the Union govt, she said.On the BJP’s approach towards TVK, Tamilisai said, “If they are soft, we will also be soft. If they are tough, we will be tough.” Political differences need not result in confrontation with the Centre over every issue, she added.
Article Summary: BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan urged the Tamil Nadu govt not to rush renovation works at Meenakshi Amman temple ahead of its consecration next month. She said shortcomings were being pointed out “out of devotion, not hostility’

Article Title: Plea seeks CBI probe into death of man after release from police custody
Article Text: Madras high court on Friday sought a report of the inquiry conducted by the magistrate in connection with the death of a 24-year-old man after his release from police custody in Thoothukudi district.
Article Summary: Madras high court on Friday sought a report of the inquiry conducted by the magistrate in connection with the death of a 24-year-old man. The man died after his release from police custody in Thoothukudi district in Tamil Nadu.

Article Title: Lady doctor arrested near Salem for illegal fetal gender determination
Article Text: SALEM: Police on Wednesday arrested a lady doctor in Vazhapadi in Salem district on charges of illegally determining and disclosing the gender of fetuses to pregnant women. Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running in the area. They sealed the clinic.Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child.Acting on a complaint, a team led by joint director Dr S P Nandhini, Attur district health officer Dr N Yoganand and Vazhapadi Government Hospital chief medical officer Dr Ramesh Kumar raided the facility.They found that Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had received Rs 30,000 from a pregnant woman to determine the gender of her fetus. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.Health department officials said this was not the first violation by the clinic. It had been raided twice earlier, and Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had faced restrictions on conducting scans and treatments, they said. Cases were registered against her then too.
Article Summary: Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running. Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.

Article Title: Kerala HC grants bail to teacher convicted in Palathayi Pocso case
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has granted bail to K Padmarajan, a former BJP leader and schoolteacher, by suspending his life sentence in the Palathayi Pocso case, in which he was accused of sexually assaulting a 10-year-old girl student multiple times inside a school bathroom in Kannur in 2020.The bench of Justices V Raja Vijayaraghavan and K V Jayakumar allowed Padmarajan’s petition seeking bail by suspending his sentence pending his appeal against the conviction and sentence. The court granted bail on the condition that he execute a bond of Rs 1 lakh with two solvent sureties and not enter the district where the survivor resides. The trial court had earlier convicted him and sentenced him to imprisonment for life for the remainder of his natural life, besides imposing a fine of Rs 1.5 lakh.While considering the application, the court observed that, prima facie, the survivor had given an inconsistent, embellished, improved and fanciful version of the alleged sexual abuse. The court also noted that the school toilet, where the alleged offences took place, was very close to the classrooms. The bench further observed that there was prima facie infirmity in the order of conviction, rendering it erroneous. Accordingly, the court granted bail to Padmarajan.
Article Summary: K Padmarajan, a former BJP leader and schoolteacher, was accused of sexually assaulting a 10-year-old girl student multiple times inside a school bathroom in Kannur in 2020. The trial court had earlier convicted him and sentenced him to imprisonment for life for the remainder of his natural life. The court granted bail on the condition that he execute a bond of Rs 1 lakh with two solvent sureties and not enter the district where the survivor resides.

Article Title: Charred remains of 58-year-old woman found at home
Article Text:
Palakkad

:





A 58-year-old woman was found dead after allegedly setting herself on fire at her home in Cherpulassery on Friday. The deceased was Leena , of Mappattukara in Kulikkallur. She was found dead at the rear of her house.Cherpulassery police have registered a case of unnatural death and launched an investigation into the circumstances leading to the incident.After completing inquest proceedings, the body was shifted to Mannarkkad taluk hospital for postmortem.
Article Summary: Leena, 58, of Mappattukara in Kulikkallur was found dead at the rear of her house. Police have registered a case of unnatural death and launched an investigation into the circumstances leading to the incident. The body was shifted to Mannarkkad taluk hospital for postmortem.

Article Title: Juvenile Justice Board to decide on custody of accused in elderly man’s murder
Article Text:
Kottayam

:





Juvenile Justice Board is set to meet on Saturday to decide on a police application seeking custody of three teenage boys taken into custody in connection with the murder of a 67-year-old man in Haripad taluk in Alappuzha.The three boys are currently lodged at the observation home in Cherthala, while a 13-year-old girl allegedly linked to the case is lodged at the observation home in Kozhikode, police said. A medical board, including a clinical psychologist, is being constituted to question the girl, police added.The funeral of the elderly man was held on Thursday evening.
Article Summary: Juvenile Justice Board is set to meet on Saturday to decide on a police application seeking custody of three teenage boys taken into custody in connection with the murder of a 67-year-old man in Haripad taluk in Alappuzha. The three boys are currently lodged at the observation home in Cherthala. A 13-year old girl allegedly linked to the case is lodged in Kozhikode.

Article Title: HC bars lawyer from courts in Kerala for illegal recording of proceedings
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Kerala High Court has barred a lawyer from participating in any court proceedings in Kerala through online or virtual mode until further orders in a contempt case over allegations that he had recorded and published the court proceedings on YouTube The bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order in a suo motu contempt case against Adv Mathew J Nedumpara and directed that a cause notice be issued to the alleged contemnor within a week. The court adjourned the case to Sept 7. The bench initiated the proceedings based on a report from the HC registry regarding the unauthorised recording and publishing of court proceedings on YouTube and X by the lawyer in a case in which he had appeared.While issuing the order, the bench observed that the alleged contemnor had been unauthorisedly recording and uploading the court proceedings on his YouTube account despite repeated warnings in the past and being fully aware that such unauthorised recording and uploading was contrary to Rule 3(9) of the Electronic Audio-Video Linkage Rules (Kerala), 2025. It further pointed out that the provision expressly prohibits broadcasting, photographing, publishing, recording or sharing proceedings conducted under the Rules, either wholly or in part, except with the written permission of the high court, court or forum.While issuing the restraining order, the bench directed that the order be circulated to the judges of the high court and district courts for information.
Article Summary: Kerala High Court has barred a lawyer from participating in any court proceedings in Kerala through online or virtual mode until further orders. The bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order in a suo motu contempt case against Adv Mathew J Nedumpara.
